meta.title: Left–right self-placement
meta.question: Do Poles place themselves on the left or on the right?
meta.measure: Placing themselves on the right, % of those leaning left or right
meta.anchor: Read on the scale of CBOS's question asking people to mark their political views on a line from left-wing (1) to right-wing (7), in its face-to-face surveys; the midpoint is left out.

items.wording: In political matters people talk of 'the left' and 'the right'. How would you place your views on this scale? (1 left, 10 right)
items.notes: Central and Eastern Eurobarometer 1-3 (1990-92). Ten points, no midpoint.
Consolidation of Democracy in Central and Eastern Europe, January 1991 and March 2000.

items.wording: Left-right self-placement of one's political views (1 left-wing, 10 right-wing)
items.notes: Polish General Social Survey, ten waves 1992-2010. In 1997-2002 asked of about half the sample.

items.wording: On this line, points mark different political views, from left-wing to right-wing. Which point best matches your own views? (1 left-wing, 7 right-wing)
items.notes: The anchor: the trend is read on this question's scale. CBOS's monthly face-to-face surveys (Aktualne problemy i wydarzenia); the midpoint, 4, is left out.

items.wording: In politics people sometimes talk of left and right. Where would you place yourself on a scale from 0 (left) to 10 (right)?
items.notes: Polish National Election Study, 1997-2023 (harmonised master file); the midpoint, 5, is left out.

items.wording: In politics people sometimes talk of 'left' and 'right'. Where would you place yourself on this scale, where 0 means the left and 10 means the right?
items.notes: European Social Survey rounds 1-11 (2002-23), respondents aged 18 and over; the midpoint, 5, is left out.

items.wording: In political matters people talk of 'the left' and 'the right'. How would you place your views on this scale? (1 left, 10 right)
In political matters people talk of 'the left' and 'the right'. How would you place your views on this scale? (1 left, 10 right)
items.notes: Standard Eurobarometer, November 2018 - November 2019, when 21-32% of Polish respondents gave no position (2-7% from 2020), so these waves have their own level.

items.wording: Where would you place your views on a scale from 0 to 10, where 0 means the left and 10 the right?
items.notes: SWPS COVID tracker, waves 9, 10 and 14 (June 2020 - July 2021); online quota samples. Wave 15 has the question but no recorded fieldwork date.

items.wording: In political matters people talk of 'the left' and 'the right'. How would you place your views on this scale? (1 left, 10 right)

As CBOS_LR, in CBOS's mixed-mode surveys (CAPI, CATI and CAWI) from May 2020; in April 2021 worded 'How would you describe your political views on a scale from 1 to 7, where 1 means left-wing and 7 right-wing?'
items.notes: Same scale; a separate level allows for the change of mode.

items.wording: In politics people sometimes talk of 'left' and 'right'. Where would you place yourself on this scale, where 0 means the left and 10 the right?
items.notes: NCN Opus panel, three waves of the same respondents (April 2023, October 2023, April 2024); online.

items.wording: In politics people sometimes talk of 'left' and 'right'. Where would you place yourself on a scale from 0 (left) to 10 (right)?
items.notes: European Election Study 2024 voter study; the midpoint, 5, is left out.

items.wording: In politics people sometimes talk of left and right. Where would you place your views on this scale? (0 left, 10 right)
items.notes: FNW SWPS surveys, May 2025, December 2025 and May 2026; online quota samples.

items.wording: Left-right self-placement (1 left-wing views, 7 right-wing views)
items.notes: PGSW 2025 presidential election study (mixed mode); the midpoint, 4, is left out.
